title: Angular-time evolution and edge-spin dynamics in the Haldane phase of the S=1 bilinear-biquadratic chain
abstract: We investigate the angular-time evolution -- a parameter-time evolution generated by the entanglement Hamiltonian -- for the bipartitioned ground state of the S=1 bilinear-biquadratic chain under the open boundary condition with the up edge spin. Using a matrix-product-state representation of the ground-state wavefunction, we calculate the angular-time spin correlation functions $\langle S_n^{α}(τ)S_{n'}^{α}(0)\rangle$ in the Haldane phase, and extract its dominant oscillation mode attributed to the nearly two-fold-degenerate entanglement spectrum associated with the $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. We also compute the effective edge-spin dynamics under a uniform magnetic field applied to the system part and numerically verify its correspondence to the dominant angular-time mode by precisely comparing the subsystem-size dependence of their amplitudes.
summary: This paper investigates the Haldane phase of the S=1 BLBQ chain by comparing two methods to study edge spin dynamics: angular-time evolution derived from the entanglement Hamiltonian, and direct simulation using an effective magnetic field. The authors successfully demonstrate that both approaches yield consistent results regarding the dominant oscillation mode, confirming a deep link between the system's entanglement structure and its boundary physics.
main_problem: The study investigates the relationship between angular-time evolution, derived from entanglement Hamiltonians, and real-time edge-spin dynamics in the Haldane phase of the S=1 bilinear-biquadratic chain.
main_result: The analysis confirms that the dominant oscillation mode extracted from both correlation functions (angular-time) and effective edge-spin protocols matches, demonstrating a robust connection between entanglement structure and boundary physics away from specific points like the AKLT limit.
method: The authors employ Matrix Product States (MPS) to calculate ground state properties, defining an angular-time evolution operator $U_l(	au) = e^{-i	au K_l}$ using the entanglement Hamiltonian $K_l$. They compare this theoretical evolution with dynamics derived from applying a uniform magnetic field to the edge spin.
model_or_system: The system is the S=1 bilinear-biquadratic (BLBQ) quantum spin chain, characterized by the Hamiltonian $H_{ eta} = \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} (S_i \cdot S_{i+1} +  eta(S_i \cdot S_{i+1})^2)$. The analysis focuses on the Haldane phase under open boundary conditions.
key_observables: Angular-time spin correlation functions $\langle S_{\alpha}^n(	au)S_{\alpha}^{n'}(0)angle$, entanglement spectrum eigenvalues ($\epsilon_i$), and effective edge-spin autocorrelation functions $G_{\alpha}^l(	au)$.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $ eta$ (ranging from 0 to approaching 1/3), the subsystem length $l$, and the correlation length $\xi$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the angular-time evolution by projecting onto the ground state sector using an approximate identity operator ($I_\chi$), which is assumed accurate away from the AKLT point.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entanglement spectrum showing bulk degeneracy and boundary splitting, compare correlation functions for different subsystem sizes ($l=6$ vs $l=40$), and show semilog plots demonstrating that amplitude decay rates are consistent between the two dynamic measurements.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the theoretical framework using MPS to define angular-time evolution via entanglement Hamiltonians. It then calculates correlation functions, compares these results against a known edge-spin protocol (magnetic field), and finally analyzes the scaling of amplitudes with subsystem size ($l$) across different coupling regimes ($ eta$).
why_interesting: The work provides a powerful theoretical tool—the angular-time evolution—to probe boundary physics in gapped quantum magnets, offering an alternative to standard real-time dynamics calculations. This connection between entanglement structure and physical observables is highly relevant for understanding topological phases.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Setup of the system and reservoir parts in the ground- state wavefunction, represented as an MPS in the mixed canonical form. The system part consists of spins i = 1 · · · l from the left edge, while the spins i > l belong to the reservoir part. A and B respectively denote the MPS tensors obtained by DMRG in the mixed canonical form, and Λ represents the singular values at the bond between sites l and l + 1.

Fig. 2. Entanglement spectrum of the bipartitioned ground- state wavefunction of the S = 1 Heisenberg chain with N = 200. The system-part length is l = 40, which is sufficiently larger than the correlation length. Accordingly, the spectrum exhibits the char- acteristic two-fold degeneracy reflecting the bulk behavior. Inset: Entanglement spectrum for l = 6, where the splitting of the two- fold degeneracy emerges due to boundary effects

Fig. 3. Angular-time correlation function Gx l (τ) and the auto- correlation function of the system-part magnetization Gx l (τ) in the effective magnetic field for the S = 1 Heisenberg chain with l = 6 and N = 200. The highly oscillatory blue curve and the gray curve represent the real parts of Gx l (τ) and Gx l (τ), respectively. The red curve shows the ω12 mode extracted from Gx l (τ) via Fourier anal- ysis.

Fig. 4. Fourier spectra of Gx l (τ) for the Heisenberg chain with N = 200, which are obtained by the Fourier transformation with the Hann window. The length of the system part is (a) l = 6 and (b) l = 40. Inset in (b) is the magnification around ω = 0, where the most dominant peaks are observed at ±ω12. Note that in the main panel of (b), these most dominant peaks ω ≃0 merge into a single peak due to limited frequency resolution.

Fig. 5. l-dependence of the amplitudes: (a) Dx l for the ω12 mode (red) and Dx l for the autocorrelation function Gx l (blue), and (b) semilog plot of |Dx l −Dx ∞| (red) and |Dx l −Dx ∞| (blue). Inset in (b): semilog plot of the amplitudes of the imaginary parts, D′x l and D′x l .
